title: Long-Acting Reversible Contraception: Insertion and Follow-Up

evidenceAudit.scope: Woman who has chosen a copper intrauterine device, a levonorgestrel intrauterine system or an etonogestrel implant in a Saudi primary care or women's health clinic: when she can start, pregnancy and infection checks, pelvic examination, pain relief, step-by-step insertion and removal, the follow-up visit, and management of bleeding, pain, missing threads, expulsion, perforation and infection. Uses the Saudi Ministry of Health Family Planning Guidelines 2023 with the US Selected Practice Recommendations 2024 and the product labels.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-14.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: The copper intrauterine device is a medical device and has no medicine label here; the Saudi guideline refers to the device listed in its Annex 8 but the licensed duration of use of the Saudi-listed copper device was not found, so no duration is written for it.

Tranexamic acid for coil-related heavy bleeding: the Saudi MOH regimen (1,500 mg three times daily for 3 days then 1,000 mg once daily for 2 days) differs from the US label for heavy menstrual bleeding (1,300 mg three times daily for up to 5 days); the Saudi regimen is written and the label dose is shown for comparison.
The US ibuprofen and acetaminophen labels are over-the-counter drug facts labels; the 200 to 400 mg and 325 to 1,000 mg pre-insertion doses are from the Saudi MOH guideline.
Misoprostol, local anaesthetic gel or paracervical block before coil insertion are not in the Saudi guideline; the Mirena label mentions a paracervical block 'if needed' and no regimen is written.
Iron tablets for anaemia are advised by the Saudi guideline but no label or regimen was reviewed.
Antibiotic treatment of pelvic inflammatory disease is referred to the sexually transmitted infection topic; no regimen is written here.
The US Selected Practice Recommendations 2024 and the labels are US sources; the Saudi guideline is followed where they differ, and the differences are shown in the comparison table.
Page numbers cited for the Saudi guideline were read from extracted PDF text and may be off by one page; check against the printed document.
Figures were read by automated extraction of PDF and label text; spot-check each dose against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: A copper device prevents fertilisation mainly by a chemical change that damages sperm and eggs; it has no hormone and does not protect against sexually transmitted infection (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 78). A levonorgestrel system releases about 21 microgram a day at first and falls to 7 microgram a day at 8 years, thickening cervical mucus and thinning the womb lining (Mirena label, Section 12). The etonogestrel implant is a single 4 cm rod that releases the hormone slowly under the skin, mainly stopping ovulation (Nexplanon label, Section 12). Perforation and expulsion are the main insertion risks and are lowest when the uterus is sounded and the device is placed high in the cavity by a trained provider (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 82; Mirena label, Section 5.5). Pelvic infection risk is concentrated in the first weeks after insertion and is higher if the woman has chlamydia or gonorrhoea at insertion (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 80). Bleeding changes are common and not harmful: heavier periods with a copper device, and irregular bleeding then light bleeding with the hormonal methods (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 88).

symptoms: Heavier or longer periods and cramping in the first 3 to 6 months with a copper device (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 78 and p. 89).
Spotting after insertion for up to the first month (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 88).
Irregular bleeding then lighter bleeding with the implant or levonorgestrel system (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 6 Implants, p. 105).
Lower abdominal pain, fever, unusual discharge or pain during sex after insertion (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 90).
physicalSigns: Threads visible at the cervix about 3 cm after cutting (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 87).
Implant palpable under the skin of the inner upper arm (Nexplanon label, Section 2.3).
Cervical motion or adnexal tenderness, purulent discharge or cervical ulcer before insertion suggest infection (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 82).
Pale conjunctivae and fatigue suggest anaemia from heavy bleeding (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 90).
redFlags: Suspected uterine perforation at insertion: stop, remove the device if inserted, bed rest and check vital signs every 5 to 10 minutes for the first hour; refer if the pulse rises, pressure falls or pain increases (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 91).

Lower abdominal pain with a missed period or abnormal bleeding with a coil or implant in place: exclude ectopic pregnancy urgently (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 90).
Fever, pelvic pain, discharge or tenderness: suspected pelvic inflammatory disease; treat or refer at once (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 90).
Pregnancy with a coil in place: remove the coil if the threads are visible and check for ectopic pregnancy (Mirena label, Section 5.1 and Section 5.2).
Implant not palpable: do not remove blindly; locate by ultrasound first and refer (Nexplanon label, Section 2.3 and Section 5.1).
Severe haemorrhage or vasovagal collapse during insertion: stop, lie flat and resuscitate (Mirena label, Section 2.2).
precipitants: Insertion within 4 weeks of childbirth other than within 48 hours (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 80 and p. 84).
Untreated chlamydia, gonorrhoea or pelvic infection at insertion (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 80 and p. 81).
Breastfeeding and insertion within 6 weeks of birth raise perforation risk (Mirena label, Section 5.5).
Distorted uterine cavity or unknown uterine position (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 82 and p. 83).
Low iron stores before a copper coil that increases bleeding (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 80).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Missed or abnormal period, positive pregnancy test, pain; always excluded before and after insertion (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 90).
Fever, discharge, cervical motion tenderness, adnexal tenderness (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 82 and p. 90).
Longer or missing threads, cramps, bleeding; partial expulsion is seen on examination or ultrasound (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 91).
Severe pain, bleeding or missing threads after insertion; ultrasound or X-ray shows a displaced device (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 91 and p. 92).

Bleeding that starts after months of normal bleeding or persists should prompt a search for polyps, fibroids, infection or cancer (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 89).

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Use with the pregnancy checklist; do not insert if pregnant (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Annex 3, p. 239; Mirena label, Section 4).

clinicalManagement.title: Counsel and check eligibility
actions: Explain effectiveness, bleeding changes, the lack of protection against sexually transmitted infections, and how long each method lasts (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 78).

Ask the medical eligibility questions about pregnancy, recent birth, post-delivery infection, unusual bleeding, genital cancer, HIV and sexually transmitted infection risk (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 80 and p. 81).
Use the pregnancy checklist; if pregnancy cannot be ruled out, do a pregnancy test (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Annex 3, p. 239).
Obtain consent and record the chosen method, the date and the planned removal date (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 88).

clinicalManagement.title: Choose the day to start
actions: Coil: any day if pregnancy is excluded; no backup within 12 days of the start of bleeding (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 83).

After birth: within 48 hours or from 4 weeks; fully breastfeeding women under 6 months can have it from 4 weeks if bleeding has not returned (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 84).
After miscarriage or abortion: immediately or within 12 days if there is no infection (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 85).
Implant: days 1 to 5 of the cycle, or any day with 7 days of backup (Nexplanon label, Section 2.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Examine the pelvis
actions: Bimanual examination for size and position of the uterus, then speculum to see the cervix (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 86).

Delay insertion and treat if there is a cervical ulcer, cervical motion tenderness, adnexal tenderness or purulent discharge (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 82).

clinicalManagement.title: Give pain relief
actions: Offer ibuprofen or paracetamol 30 minutes before insertion; do not give aspirin (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 86).
Describe each step and ask her to say if she has pain (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 86).

clinicalManagement.title: Insert the device
actions: Use infection prevention measures, clean the cervix, steady it with a tenaculum, and sound the uterus (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 86).

Load the device in its sterile package, insert to the fundus, withdraw the inserter and cut the threads to about 3 cm (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 87).
For the levonorgestrel system follow the label steps and sound to 6 to 10 cm (Mirena label, Section 2.2).
For the implant anaesthetise the track, insert subdermally on the inner non-dominant upper arm and confirm by palpation (Nexplanon label, Section 2.2).
Let her rest on the couch until she feels ready to dress (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 87).

clinicalManagement.title: Give after-care and a reminder card
actions: Expect cramping and spotting for a few days; use ibuprofen or paracetamol (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 88).
Give a reminder card with the device type, insertion date, removal date and where to go with problems (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 88).
Advise condoms against sexually transmitted infection and explain the warning signs (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 90).

clinicalManagement.title: Follow up and manage problems
clinicalManagement.timeframe: After the first period or 3 to 6 weeks
actions: Review after the first period or 3 to 6 weeks; do not refuse a device because follow-up may be difficult (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 88).

Heavy bleeding: reassure, try tranexamic acid or a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug, check haemoglobin and give iron (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 89 and p. 90).

Partial expulsion: remove the device and offer a new one or another method; missing threads: backup method and ultrasound (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 91).
Pelvic inflammatory disease: treat; the device need not be removed unless she wishes or there is no improvement (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 90).
At removal use narrow forceps and pull the threads gently; fertility returns immediately (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 87 and p. 78).

regimens.indication: Pain relief before coil or implant insertion and for cramping afterwards
regimens.patientGroup: Adult women having a coil or implant inserted
regimens.dose: 200 to 400 mg once, 30 minutes before insertion; afterwards 200 to 400 mg as needed (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 86 and p. 88). Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablet.
regimens.route: Oral, swallowed with water; take with food or milk if the stomach is upset (Ibuprofen label, Directions)
regimens.frequency: Once before insertion; then every 4 to 6 hours as needed
regimens.duration: Usually 1 to 2 days after insertion; stop and ask a doctor if pain lasts more than 10 days (Ibuprofen label, Stop use)
adjustments: Do not use aspirin before insertion because it slows clotting (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 86).
Avoid in the last half of pregnancy; not relevant here but exclude pregnancy first (Ibuprofen label, Pregnancy).
Take the lowest effective dose and the shortest time (Ibuprofen label, Directions).

SFDA: this exact product is not listed in Annex 8 of the Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023 and the live SFDA register could not be opened, so registration in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check before prescribing.
monitoring: Stomach pain, black stools or vomiting blood: stop and seek care (Ibuprofen label, Stop use).
Severe or persistent cramping beyond 2 days: examine for partial expulsion or perforation (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 89).
contraindications: Previous allergic reaction to ibuprofen or other pain relievers, including aspirin-triggered asthma (Ibuprofen label, Do not use).
Right before or after heart surgery (Ibuprofen label, Do not use).
Ask a doctor first with stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, liver cirrhosis or a diuretic (Ibuprofen label, Ask a doctor before use).
regimens.useWhen: Preferred first choice as listed in the Saudi guideline.
regimens.sourceTitle: Ibuprofen 200 mg tablets (NSAID): US drug facts label (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 86 to p. 88; Ibuprofen label, Section Directions

regimens.indication: Pain relief before coil or implant insertion for women who cannot take an anti-inflammatory tablet
regimens.patientGroup: Adult women unable to take a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug
regimens.dose: 325 to 1,000 mg once, 30 minutes before insertion (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 86). Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablet.
regimens.frequency: Once before insertion; then 1,000 mg every 6 hours as needed
regimens.duration: Usually 1 to 2 days; no more than 10 days unless directed (Acetaminophen label, Directions)
adjustments: Do not exceed 4,000 mg of acetaminophen in 24 hours; the 500 mg over-the-counter label limits to 6 tablets (3,000 mg) a day (Acetaminophen label, Warnings and Directions).
Do not take with any other acetaminophen-containing product (Acetaminophen label, Do not use).
Warfarin users should ask a doctor or pharmacist (Acetaminophen label, Ask a doctor or pharmacist).

SFDA: this exact product is not listed in Annex 8 of the Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023 and the live SFDA register could not be opened, so registration in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check before prescribing.
monitoring: Skin reaction: stop and seek care (Acetaminophen label, Allergy alert).
Liver injury risk with alcohol and overdose (Acetaminophen label, Liver warning).
contraindications: Allergy to acetaminophen or an inactive ingredient (Acetaminophen label, Do not use).
Liver disease: ask a doctor before use (Acetaminophen label, Ask a doctor before use).
regimens.useWhen: Choose when ibuprofen is not suitable (ulcer, kidney disease, aspirin-sensitive asthma).
regimens.sourceTitle: Acetaminophen (paracetamol) 500 mg tablets: US drug facts label (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 86; Acetaminophen label, Section Directions

regimens.indication: Local anaesthesia of the implant insertion track
regimens.patientGroup: Women having an etonogestrel implant inserted
regimens.dose: 2 mL of 1% lidocaine injected just under the skin along the planned insertion track, or an anaesthetic spray (Nexplanon label, Section 2.2). Dilution and preparation: none; use the 1% solution as supplied.
regimens.route: Subcutaneous infiltration along the insertion tunnel; aspirate before injecting (Nexplanon label, Section 2.2; Xylocaine label, Warnings)
adjustments: Confirm no allergy to the anaesthetic or antiseptic first (Nexplanon label, Section 2.2).
Do not exceed the label maximum dose (Xylocaine label, Dosage and Administration).

SFDA: this exact product is not listed in Annex 8 of the Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023 and the live SFDA register could not be opened, so registration in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check before prescribing.
monitoring: Signs of toxicity: perioral numbness, dizziness, tinnitus, convulsions (Xylocaine label, Adverse Reactions).
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to amide-type local anaesthetics (Xylocaine label, Contraindications).
regimens.sourceEdition: Nexplanon label, Section 2.2; Xylocaine label, Section Contraindications

regimens.indication: Prevention of pregnancy for up to 5 years with one implant
regimens.patientGroup: Women wanting the most effective method, including breastfeeding women and women who cannot use estrogen
regimens.dose: One 68 mg etonogestrel rod, 4 cm long, in a preloaded applicator. Dilution and preparation: none; check the rod is visible in the needle tip before insertion.
regimens.route: Subdermal insertion into the inner side of the non-dominant upper arm over the triceps, 8 to 10 cm above the medial epicondyle and 3 to 5 cm behind the groove between biceps and triceps, by a trained and certified provider; palpate the implant straight away and ask the woman to feel it (Nexplanon label, Section 2.2)
regimens.duration: Remove by the end of the labelled duration (up to 5 years on the US label) and replace if still wanted (Nexplanon label, Section 1 and Section 2.4)
adjustments: Insert on days 1 to 5 of the cycle with no backup; at other times exclude pregnancy and add a barrier method for 7 days (Nexplanon label, Section 2.1).
Postpartum and breastfeeding: any time up to 6 months with no backup if bleeding has not returned (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 6 Implants, p. 105).
Deep insertion can cause nerve or vessel injury and make removal difficult (Nexplanon label, Section 5.1 and Section 5.2).
Enzyme-inducing medicines may reduce effect; add a barrier method (Nexplanon label, Section 7).

SFDA: listed in Annex 8 of the Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023 (drugs registered in the Saudi Food and Drug Authority); the live SFDA register could not be opened from this environment, so current registration was not re-checked.
monitoring: Palpate at every review; if not palpable, locate by ultrasound before any removal (Nexplanon label, Section 2.3).
Bleeding pattern changes are the commonest reason for removal (Nexplanon label, Section 5.3).
Ectopic pregnancy, ovarian cysts, blood pressure and mood (Nexplanon label, Section 5.4 and Section 5.10).
contraindications: Known or suspected pregnancy (Nexplanon label, Section 4).
Current or past thrombosis or thromboembolic disorder (Nexplanon label, Section 4).
Liver tumour or active liver disease (Nexplanon label, Section 4).
Undiagnosed abnormal uterine bleeding (Nexplanon label, Section 4).
Known or suspected breast cancer or other progestin-sensitive cancer; allergy to any component (Nexplanon label, Section 4).
regimens.sourceEdition: Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 6 Implants, p. 103 to p. 106; Nexplanon US label, Section 2.1 to Section 2.4 and Section 4

regimens.indication: Prevention of pregnancy for up to 8 years with one hormonal coil (also treats heavy menstrual bleeding)
regimens.patientGroup: Women wanting a long-acting method, especially with heavy periods
regimens.dose: One levonorgestrel 52 mg intrauterine system releasing about 21 microgram per day at first, falling to about 7 microgram per day at 8 years. Dilution and preparation: none; supplied sterile in an inserter, open only at insertion.
regimens.route: Intrauterine insertion by a trained provider using strict aseptic technique and the single-handed inserter after sounding the uterus to 6 to 10 cm; set the flange to the sounded depth; wait 10 seconds for the arms to open; advance to the fundus, release and withdraw the inserter; cut the threads (Mirena label, Section 2.2)
regimens.duration: Up to 8 years for contraception; remove and replace at the end of that period (Mirena label, Section 1 and Section 2.1)
adjustments: Insert in the first 7 days of the cycle with no backup, or at any time pregnancy is excluded with a barrier method or abstinence for 7 days (Mirena label, Section 2.2).

After childbirth: within 48 hours with a trained provider, or wait at least 4 weeks (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Levonorgestrel Intrauterine Device, p. 97); the US label says wait at least 6 weeks and warns of higher perforation risk in breastfeeding women (Mirena label, Section 2.2 and Section 5.5).
Immediately after a first-trimester abortion or miscarriage if not septic (Mirena label, Section 2.2).

SFDA: listed in Annex 8 of the Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023 (drugs registered in the Saudi Food and Drug Authority); the live SFDA register could not be opened from this environment, so current registration was not re-checked.
monitoring: Review 4 to 6 weeks after insertion and yearly (Mirena label, Section 2.3).
Pelvic pain, fever or foul discharge after insertion: examine for pelvic infection (Mirena label, Section 5.3 and Section 5.4).
Missing threads: ultrasound to exclude expulsion or perforation (Mirena label, Section 5.5 and Section 5.6).
contraindications: Pregnancy or suspected pregnancy; not for emergency contraception (Mirena label, Section 4).
Uterine anomaly or fibroids that distort the cavity (Mirena label, Section 4).
Acute pelvic inflammatory disease or recent postpartum endometritis or infected abortion; untreated acute cervicitis or vaginitis (Mirena label, Section 4).
Known or suspected uterine or cervical cancer, breast cancer or other progestin-sensitive cancer; uterine bleeding of unknown cause (Mirena label, Section 4).
Acute liver disease or liver tumour; a previously inserted coil not removed; hypersensitivity (Mirena label, Section 4).
regimens.sourceTitle: MIRENA (levonorgestrel intrauterine system): US prescribing information (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Levonorgestrel Intrauterine Device, p. 95 to p. 99; Mirena US label, Section 1, Section 2.1 to Section 2.3, Section 4 and Section 5

regimens.indication: Short-term relief of heavy or prolonged bleeding with a copper coil
regimens.patientGroup: Women with a copper coil and heavy bleeding after serious causes are excluded
regimens.dose: 1,500 mg three times daily for 3 days, then 1,000 mg once daily for 2 days, starting when heavy bleeding starts (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 89); the US label dose for heavy menstrual bleeding is 1,300 mg three times daily for a maximum of 5 days (Tranexamic acid tablets label, Section 2.1). Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablets, swallow whole.
regimens.route: Oral, with or without food, swallowed whole; do not chew (Tranexamic acid tablets label, Section 2.1)
regimens.frequency: Three times daily for 3 days, then once daily for 2 days
regimens.duration: 5 days at the start of heavy bleeding, one try at a time
adjustments: Renal impairment: reduce the dose according to serum creatinine (Tranexamic acid tablets label, Section 2.3).
Exclude endometrial pathology before prescribing for heavy menstrual bleeding (Tranexamic acid tablets label, Section 2.1).
Not to be used with combined hormonal contraception; a copper coil is hormone-free (Tranexamic acid tablets label, Section 4.1).

SFDA: this exact product is not listed in Annex 8 of the Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023 and the live SFDA register could not be opened, so registration in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check before prescribing.
monitoring: Signs of thrombosis: leg swelling, chest pain, vision loss (Tranexamic acid tablets label, Section 5.1).
Allergic reaction (Tranexamic acid tablets label, Section 5.2).
Haemoglobin if bleeding persists (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 90).
contraindications: Active thromboembolic disease or a history of thrombosis, including retinal vein or artery occlusion (Tranexamic acid tablets label, Section 4.1).
Intrinsic risk of thrombosis such as thrombogenic valvular or rhythm disease or hypercoagulopathy (Tranexamic acid tablets label, Section 4.1).
Use of combined hormonal contraception (Tranexamic acid tablets label, Section 4.1).
Known hypersensitivity to tranexamic acid (Tranexamic acid tablets label, Section 4.2).

adjustments: Do not use aspirin; indomethacin 25 mg twice daily is the other listed option (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 89).
Take the lowest effective dose for the shortest time (Ibuprofen label, Directions).

SFDA: this exact product is not listed in Annex 8 of the Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023 and the live SFDA register could not be opened, so registration in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check before prescribing.
monitoring: Stomach pain, black stools or vomiting blood: stop and seek care (Ibuprofen label, Stop use).
Bleeding that persists or begins after months of normal bleeding: look for another cause (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 89).
contraindications: Previous allergic reaction to ibuprofen or other pain relievers (Ibuprofen label, Do not use).
Right before or after heart surgery (Ibuprofen label, Do not use).
Ask a doctor first with stomach ulcer, kidney disease, heart disease or high blood pressure (Ibuprofen label, Ask a doctor before use).

branches.entryCriteria: Woman who chose an etonogestrel implant, not pregnant, no thrombosis, active liver disease or undiagnosed bleeding, and no allergy to the antiseptic or local anaesthetic.

All doses are for adult women. Copper device: medical device with no medicine label.

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Reasonably certain she is not pregnant
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Pregnancy checklist answered 'yes' to at least one question, or a negative test with the checklist (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Annex 3, p. 239).

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Start of a coil in a woman with periods
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Any day if pregnancy is excluded; no backup if within 12 days of the start of bleeding (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 83).
Within 48 hours, or from 4 weeks (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 84).

Infection after childbirth or abortion, unexplained bleeding, genital cancer or pelvic tuberculosis, severe HIV disease, very high sexually transmitted infection risk without testing (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 80 and p. 81).
Within 5 days of the start of bleeding with no backup, or any time pregnancy is excluded with 7 days of backup (Nexplanon label, Section 2.1).
After the first period or 3 to 6 weeks after coil insertion (Saudi MOH Family Planning Guidelines 2023, Chapter 5 Intrauterine Devices, p. 88).

teaching.scope: Woman who has chosen a copper intrauterine device, a levonorgestrel intrauterine system or an etonogestrel implant in a Saudi primary care or women's health clinic: when she can start, pregnancy and infection checks, pelvic examination, pain relief, step-by-step insertion and removal, the follow-up visit, and management of bleeding, pain, missing threads, expulsion, perforation and infection. Uses the Saudi Ministry of Health Family Planning Guidelines 2023 with the US Selected Practice Recommendations 2024 and the product labels.
learningObjectives: Rule out pregnancy and infection and examine the pelvis before insertion.
Give pain relief 30 minutes before and explain each step.
Insert at the fundus by a trained provider and confirm the implant by palpation.
Review after the first period or 3 to 6 weeks and manage bleeding and pain.
pitfalls: Failing to give a reminder card and explain warning signs.
keyPoints: Do not insert within 48 hours to 4 weeks after childbirth.
Do not insert with active pelvic infection, unexplained bleeding or an unsoundable uterus.
Use ibuprofen or paracetamol, not aspirin, before insertion.
A non-palpable implant needs ultrasound before removal.

patientEducation: Cramps and spotting are normal for a few days.
Periods may be heavier with a copper coil; they usually settle in 3 to 6 months.
Return if you have fever, severe pain, foul discharge, a missed period or cannot feel the threads or the implant.
Condoms are still needed to protect against infections.
Keep your card and return for removal or replacement on the date shown.
Your fertility returns as soon as the device is removed.
lifestyleAndDiet: Eat iron-rich food such as meat, fish, green vegetables and legumes.
Rest on the day of insertion.
Do not use tampons or have sex for 24 hours if advised locally.
Check threads monthly if you were shown how.
Use condoms with a new partner.
mdtReferrals: Primary care physician or family physician; trained nurse or midwife; obstetrician and gynaecologist; sonographer; sexual health team; pharmacist.
dischargeCriteria: Method, date of insertion and removal date recorded; reminder card given; pain relief advised; warning signs and follow-up date explained; condoms advised.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review after the first period or 3 to 6 weeks for coils; palpate the implant at every review; yearly review for blood pressure and bleeding; remove or replace on the due date.
